title: Grateful Dead Live at Dance Hall on 1967-09-03

ai_review.summary: Raw, exploratory 9/3/67 show captured from a soundboard with cuts but still delivers a historic Viola Lee jam and high‑energy psychedelic blues.
ai_review.review: The performance is celebrated for its youthful, experimental vibe – especially the extended Viola Lee Blues and the marathon Midnight Hour – even if the band isn’t always tight. The soundboard source suffers noticeable edits and occasional phasing, yet it remains one of the better‑preserved snapshots of the Dead’s formative 1967 era.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is rated high by most reviewers (average ~4.2) while recording quality is mixed due to cuts and occasional muddiness (~3). Weighted combination yields a solid 3.8‑star rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Several cuts and missing sections are noted; Alligator shows phasing/flutter, Viola Lee is a bit muddled, but overall the soundboard capture is decent for a 1967 recording.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑67 set with long, exploratory jams and repetitive riffs; historic first‑era material that feels raw and adventurous despite occasional looseness.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s bluesy lead work is praised as soulful and deep, especially on extended jam sections.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass underpins the improvisations; he later recalled the gig fondly, highlighting his central role in this early performance.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ (P.P.) is prominent and raw; Brent’s keyboard contributions are noted with a vivid quote about his attitude.
